content.text:
I submitted **index 142** (Cr 0.067, Fe 0.449, V 0.484). At 1.1×10⁻⁷ A it had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured.

| Index | Cr | Fe | V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 127 | 0.20 | 0.32 | 0.48 | 5×10⁻⁸ |
| 0 | 0.097 | 0.41 | 0.49 | 7×10⁻⁸ |
| 142 | 0.067 | 0.45 | 0.48 | 1.1×10⁻⁷ |

I only had three merit measurements. I kept all three near FeVO4 proportions (Fe + Cr about equal to V, each around 0.5), a known photoanode material, and lowered the Cr each time. Photocurrent rose every time Cr went down. With three points that's a trend, not a firm result. The Fe-rich and V-rich parts of the library were never measured, so a better composition could be there.

- **No XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so it's untested whether the films actually have the FeVO4 structure.
- **Phase list not read:** the known-phase list was too large to load, so I didn't use it.
- **GP not followed:** after two points the model's suggestions all predicted lower photocurrents than I had already measured. I used the last measurement on the lowest-Cr candidate instead.
